summary: Phase 1 passes acceptance at 0db45c6. All three tasks have SHA evidence, and the focus criterion holds in the tests and in the live check. The tsc run, the vitest run, and the bundle comparison pass. Three nonblocking Nits remain.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] phase-acceptance: FR-3 says a pending paint runs when an empty box loses focus. No live check covers this, and the unit test calls flush() directly (src/painter-dom.test.ts:373-376). In Chrome, document.activeElement is body inside a blur handler, so the flush() at panel/main.ts:399 can repaint during the focus change. That repaint can remove the pressed control and lose the click or Tab target. When the whole frame loses focus, document.activeElement stays on the textarea, so holdComment (src/painter.ts:87) keeps holding. Rationale: FR-3 requires the blur flush, so no spec breach exists, but a first click can be lost.

F2 [Nit] phase-acceptance: Static review finds no test that asserts the preventScroll argument at src/painter.ts:104. It finds no test that shows restoreComment leaves focus alone when the box had none or the snapshot key differs (src/painter.ts:103). It finds no pin for capture-before-render in panel/main.ts:288-299. The test at src/painter-dom.test.ts:138-149 uses the constant '   '.length > 0 as its hold, so it proves nothing about whitespace. The headers at src/painter.test.ts:4-5 and src/painter-dom.test.ts:4-5 still say the suite fails until src/painter.ts exists. Rationale: FR-1 and FR-5 name these rules, so a regression could pass the full suite.

F3 [Nit] phase-acceptance: plan.md lines 13 and 17 write counts: 2 errors, 21 suites, 308 tests, 268 samples, and 230 samples. The rule in skills/measure-orchestrator/SKILL.md says to write no count in plan.md and to cite the log file. The counts are true and match red-p1.log, timer-72s.json, and host-reply-60s.json, so no A5 mismatch exists. Rationale: the same rule names a pinned count as the most common cause of record-fix rounds.
